h: Broad Street Tactics for a Winning Night
p: Broad Street has been a big name in Birmingham's nightlife for years, linking the city centre with the canal side developments around Brindleyplace and the Mailbox. These days it's more mixed than its old party-strip reputation suggests, with bars, restaurants, hotels and big venues all crammed along it. A games bar fits neatly into that: you get a plan, a focus and a bit of rivalry before you hit the rest of the night.

The trams make getting here easy, with the Midland Metro running along Broad Street and linking up with New Street and Grand Central. If you're coming from further out, Birmingham's rail connections mean groups can arrive from London, Manchester and the rest of the Midlands without too much fuss. For anyone staying over, there are plenty of hotels within a short walk.

The best nights at a place like this usually follow a simple plan. Pick your games early, decide on teams, and keep the scoreboard on display so nobody can quietly forget a loss. If you've got a big group, splitting into two or three smaller teams keeps everyone involved and avoids people standing around. And if someone's not a drinker, games bars are a great leveller, as the fun doesn't depend on how many rounds you've had.

For a daytime warm-up, the National SEA LIFE Centre at Brindleyplace is close by, as is the Ikon Gallery in its old Victorian school building, so you can easily fit something calmer in before the battles start.
